paper.citation: R. Ganardi, T. V. Kondra, N. H. Y. Ng, A. Streltsov, Second Law of Entanglement Manipulation with an Entanglement Battery, Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 010202 (2025)

phases: a new operation class, LOCC with a battery, is proposed
the process layer gains a node that is defined through a quantifier
conversion rates E(ρ)/E(σ) for every pair of states

nodes.label: Battery states τ, τ~ (entanglement battery)
nodes.def: Bipartite states of an auxiliary system A'B' (or C); τ before, τ~ after the protocol; not fixed in advance.

nodes.label: Pair (ρ_PPT, σ_ε) (order-reversal example)
nodes.def: ρ_PPT: a PPT entangled state; σ_ε = √(1−ε)|00> + √ε|11> with small ε.

nodes.label: Additivity of E (Eq. (12))
nodes.def: E(ρ^{AB}⊗σ^{A'B'}) = E(ρ^{AB}) + E(σ^{A'B'}) for all states.

nodes.label: LOCC monotonicity of E
nodes.def: E(Λ[ρ]) ≤ E(ρ) for every LOCC protocol Λ.

nodes.label: Finiteness of E
nodes.def: E(ρ) is a real number for every state (no value +∞).

nodes.label: Asymptotic continuity of E (Eq. (13), generalised)
nodes.def: |E(ρ) − E(σ)| ≤ g(‖ρ−σ‖₁)·log2 d + f(‖ρ−σ‖₁) with g, f → 0 at 0, f independent of d. Eq. (13) is the case g(x) = Kx.

nodes.label: LOCC with an entanglement battery, relative to E
nodes.def: ρ → σ iff there are τ, τ~ and an LOCC protocol Λ with Λ(ρ⊗τ) = σ⊗τ~ and E(τ~) ≥ E(τ) (Eqs. (9)–(10)); asymptotic version Eqs. (11a)–(11d).

nodes.label: Operations form a class of channels (premise of the no-go for non-entangling operations)
nodes.def: The allowed operations are a set of channels on the system, fixed independently of the input state and containing no channel that maps a separable state to an entangled one.

nodes.label: Thermal operations with a free-energy battery
nodes.def: (ρ,H_S) → (σ,H_S') iff a thermal operation maps ρ⊗τ to σ⊗τ~ with F(τ~) ≥ F(τ).

nodes.label: Quantifier E (admissible class)
nodes.def: A function on bipartite states satisfying ax-add, ax-mono, ax-fin (and ax-ac for Theorem 2).

nodes.label: Squashed entanglement E_sq
nodes.def: E_sq(ρ^{AB}) = inf{ I(A;B|E)/2 : ρ^{ABE} an extension of ρ^{AB} } (Eq. (5)).

nodes.label: Geometric entanglement E_g
nodes.def: E_g(ψ) = 1 − max over product states of |<a,b|ψ>|².

nodes.label: Single-copy conversion ρ → σ
nodes.def: Existence of a battery-assisted protocol producing σ exactly from one copy of ρ.

nodes.label: Asymptotic rate R(ρ → σ)
nodes.def: Supremum of r such that for all ε, δ > 0 there are n, m with m/n > r − δ and a protocol satisfying (11a)–(11c); zero-error version with ε = 0.

nodes.label: Reversibility of entanglement manipulation
nodes.def: R(ρ→σ)·R(σ→ρ) = 1 for all pairs of states with 0 < E < ∞.

edges.statement: Definition of battery-assisted LOCC: the operation class is defined through the quantifier E.
edges.note: Signature M∧O∧S→M: an operation class defined through an observable-layer node. In the released resource-theory network v1.2 no operation class is defined this way; its one witness→process edge (W15) is a bound, not a definition.

edges.statement: If ρ → σ under battery-assisted LOCC then E(ρ) ≥ E(σ).
edges.check: SMT (linear real arithmetic): the four premises entail E(σ) ≤ E(ρ); each premise is needed (4/4 — dropping any one admits a counter-model)

edges.statement: If E(ρ) ≥ E(σ) then ρ → σ: take τ = σ and swap A↔A', B↔B'; then τ~ = ρ.
edges.scope: instances: (dA,dB) = (2,2), (2,3) for the permutation identity (an index identity valid in every dimension)
edges.check: exact: the product of Alice's swap A↔A' and Bob's swap B↔B' maps X^{AB}⊗Y^{A'B'} to Y^{AB}⊗X^{A'B'} for symbolic X, Y; SMT: with τ = σ the battery condition is E(ρ) ≥ E(σ)

edges.statement: ρ → σ under battery-assisted LOCC iff E(ρ) ≥ E(σ).
edges.check: SMT: the two implications give the equivalence
SMT: induction step holds (base case k = 1 is trivial); the induction schema itself is not a kernel rule

edges.statement: Zero-error rates satisfy m/n ≤ E(ρ)/E(σ).
edges.check: SMT (nonlinear real arithmetic): m/n ≤ E(ρ)/E(σ); every premise needed

edges.statement: Every pair (n, m) with m E(σ) ≤ n E(ρ) is achieved exactly by relabelling, with battery σ^{⊗m} → ρ^{⊗n}.
edges.check: SMT: for every pair (n, m) with m E(σ) ≤ n E(ρ) the relabelling of the n source copies and the m battery copies satisfies the battery condition; output is exactly σ^{⊗m} (zero error)

edges.statement: Rational rates m/n approach E(ρ)/E(σ) from below.
edges.check: SMT: with m = ⌊n x⌋ and n ≥ 1/δ one has x − δ < m/n ≤ x; existence of the floor is the Archimedean property of the reals (library fact)

edges.statement: R_ze(ρ → σ) = E(ρ)/E(σ) for additive, monotone, finite E with E(σ) > 0.
edges.check: SMT: upper bound and approximation from below force R_ze = E(ρ)/E(σ) (the quantifiers over δ are instantiated by hand, as shown in the premises)

edges.statement: With error ε: m/n ≤ (E(ρ) + f(ε)/n)/(E(σ) − g(ε) log2 d) whenever g(ε) log2 d < E(σ).
edges.check: SMT: m/n ≤ (E(ρ) + f/n)/(E(σ) − x) for any modulus x = g(ε)·log2 d with x < E(σ); Eq. (23) is the case g(ε) = Kε; every premise needed

edges.statement: The bound of GB9 converges to E(ρ)/E(σ) as ε → 0.
edges.where: Eq. (25) and the sentence after it
edges.check: SMT: for every η > 0, once x and f are below explicit thresholds the right-hand side of (23) is at most E(ρ)/E(σ) + η; since g(ε), f(ε) → 0 this gives R ≤ E(ρ)/E(σ)

edges.statement: R(ρ → σ) = E(ρ)/E(σ) for finite, additive, monotone, asymptotically continuous E.
edges.check: SMT: converse (for every η) and achievability (for every δ) force R = E(ρ)/E(σ) (quantifiers instantiated by hand, as shown in the premises)
edges.note: A zero-error protocol is in particular an ε-error protocol, so GB6 and GB7 give achievability.

edges.check: SMT: (E(ρ)/E(σ))·(E(σ)/E(ρ)) = 1 for positive finite values

edges.statement: E_sq is additive on tensor products and does not increase under LOCC.
edges.note: Monotonicity is needed (GB1) and has no dedicated citation in the paper; it is proved in the same reference [from knowledge].

edges.statement: E_sq(ρ) = 0 iff ρ is separable; E_sq is finite; E_sq of a pure state is the entropy of entanglement.
|E_sq(ρ) − E_sq(σ)| ≤ 16√(2ε) log d + 4h(2√(2ε)) for trace distance ≤ ε.
refs: Alicki, Fannes, J. Phys. A 37, L55 (2004), arXiv:quant-ph/0312081
edges.note: The modulus is proportional to √ε. This satisfies ax-ac in the generalised form used by GB9, not the linear form of Eq. (13) as printed.

edges.statement: E_g(ψ_d^{⊗n}) = E_g(φ+^{⊗n}) = 1 − 2^{−n} while S(ψ_d^A) = 1 + ½ log2(d−1); E_g is not additive.
edges.check: exact (symbolic d, n): Schmidt spectrum {1/2, 1/(2(d−1)) × (d−1)}; E_g equal to that of a Bell state for every number of copies, entropy of entanglement unbounded in d; E_g violates Eq. (12)

edges.statement: With E = E_g the battery condition permits φ+^{⊗n} → ψ_d^{⊗n} for every d, hence unbounded singlet yield.
edges.check: GB14 (equal E_g for every n; entropy unbounded in d) and GB2 (swap protocol) give φ+^{⊗n} → ψ_d^{⊗n}; GB15i then distils ψ_d^{⊗n} to singlets at rate S(ψ_d^A), which exceeds any bound for large d

edges.statement: Pure states are distilled to singlets by LOCC at rate S(ψ^A).
edges.where: Ref. [8], section on asymptotic transformations; used after Eq. (84)
refs: Bennett, Bernstein, Popescu, Schumacher, Phys. Rev. A 53, 2046 (1996)

edges.statement: ‖(|φ+><φ+|)^{T_A}‖₁ = 2; for σ_ε the trace norm is 1 + 2√(ε(1−ε)).
edges.check: exact: the partial transpose of √(1−ε)|00>+√ε|11> has eigenvalues 1−ε, ε, ±√(ε(1−ε)); trace norm 1 + 2√(ε(1−ε)), equal to 2 for the Bell state, so E_N(φ+) = 1 and E_N > 0 for all 0 < ε < 1

edges.statement: With error ε the singlet rate under the E_N battery obeys m/n ≤ E_N(ρ) − (1/n)log2(1−ε).
E_N is additive and LOCC monotone; ‖X^{T_A}‖₁ ≤ d_A‖X‖₁ (Eq. (76)).
(ρ,H) → (σ,H') with thermal operations and a free-energy battery iff F(ρ,H) ≥ F(σ,H').
edges.check: SMT: the two directions of Theorem 1 with F in place of E

edges.statement: F is additive over non-interacting systems, non-increasing under thermal operations, finite for 0 < T < ∞; swapping system and battery with their Hamiltonians is a thermal operation.
The states reachable from separable states are exactly those with E = 0.
edges.where: main text, paragraph comparing with Ref. [7]
edges.check: SMT: σ is reachable from a separable state iff E(σ) = 0
edges.note: For E_sq the zero set is SEP (GB13b). For E_N it is the set of PPT states, so the E_N battery allows bound entangled states to be made from separable ones.

edges.statement: The pre-orders induced by E_sq and by E_N disagree on (ρ_PPT, σ_ε): each allows the conversion the other forbids.
edges.where: consequence of Theorem 1; main text: a different quantifier gives a different second law
edges.scope: general (given the imported properties of E_sq and the existence of PPT entangled states)
edges.check: exact + SMT: h(ε) → 0 as ε → 0+ and E_N(σ_ε) > 0; hence for small ε the E_N battery allows σ_ε → ρ_PPT and forbids ρ_PPT → σ_ε, while the E_sq battery does the reverse

edges.statement: PPT entangled states exist.
Under non-entangling operations, a fixed class of channels, entanglement manipulation is irreversible.
The pair (swap, τ = σ) induces the replacement channel X ↦ σ on the system and is admitted only for inputs with E(ρ) ≥ E(σ): battery-assisted LOCC is not a class of non-entangling channels.
edges.where: main text, paragraph comparing with Ref. [7]: the operation may depend on the initial and final states
edges.scope: instances: dA = dB = 2 for the partial-trace identity (valid in every dimension)
edges.check: exact: tracing the battery out of the swapped state gives σ·tr X for every input X, so the induced channel on the system is the replacement channel X ↦ σ, which maps separable inputs to the entangled target; SMT: for an input with E(ρ') < E(σ) the same pair (Λ, τ) violates the battery condition

edges.statement: GB12 (reversibility) does not contradict the irreversibility under non-entangling operations.
edges.check: scope separation: no-go GB21i needs premise ax-chan; possibility GB12 does not use it; GB21e certifies its absence

edges.statement: Battery-assisted LOCC is not catalysis: the battery may change state; only E(τ~) ≥ E(τ) is required.

operations.why: new operation class; closes the entanglement row of gap QG9 ('entanglement-battery second law, arXiv:2405.10599 [verify]')
the quantifier that makes Theorems 1–2 non-vacuous; currently absent from wQ-ent
AND route into a process node with a witness-layer leg: the first operation class in the resource-theory network that is defined through a quantifier

operations.edge: p-bat —reversible→ sR-ent (rate E(ρ)/E(σ); via LOCC + battery relative to E)
operations.why: Theorem 2; kernel-checked modulo the imported properties of E

operations.note: 'no single monotone can govern all transformations' holds for LOCC and for non-entangling operations; under p-bat(E) the single monotone E governs all transformations by construction
replace 'candidate route around pX-ent via entanglement batteries (QG9)' by the theorem, with the distinction battery ≠ catalyst (GB22)
citation verified: Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 010202 (2025), DOI 10.1103/kl56-p2vb
full additivity of the regularised relative entropy of entanglement is stated as unknown in the paper; if it held, p-bat(E_r^∞) would reproduce the rate of F-STEIN
